audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet siege-release oracle, four excluded men, abandoned Aramean camp, public announcement, and gate-officer death narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for impossible-price oracle, skeptical officer, four men with skin disease at the gate, hunger-risk decision, panic in Aramean camp, abandoned wealth and food, concealment then disclosure, cautious reconnaissance, famine relief, crowd crush, and fulfilled warning.

verses.restored: Elisha said, Hear word of YHWH: Thus says YHWH, About this time tomorrow a seah of fine flour shall be for one shekel and two seahs of barley for one shekel at gate of Samaria.

familiar.text: Then Elisha said, Hear ye the word of the LORD; Thus saith the LORD, To morrow about this time shall a measure of fine flour be sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.

modern.text: Then Elisha said, “Hear the word of the LORD! This is what the LORD says: ‘About this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria, a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר יְהוָ֑ה כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה כָּעֵ֤ת מָחָר֙ סְאָֽה סֹ֣לֶת בְּשֶׁ֗קֶל וְסָאתַ֧יִם שְׂעֹרִ֛ים בְּשֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשַׁ֥עַר שֹׁמְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: The officer on whose hand king leaned answered man of Divine and said, Look, if YHWH made windows in heavens, could this thing be? He said, Look, you shall see it with your eyes, but from there you shall not eat.

familiar.text: Then a lord on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God, and said, Behold, if the LORD would make windows in heaven, might this thing be? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.

modern.text: But the officer on whose arm the king leaned answered the man of God, “Look, even if the LORD were to make windows in heaven, could this really happen?” “You will see it with your own eyes,” replied Elisha, “but you will not eat any of it.” The Syrians Flee

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַן הַשָּׁלִ֡ישׁ אֲשֶׁר לַמֶּלֶךְ֩ נִשְׁעָ֨ן עַל יָד֜וֹ אֶת אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ הִנֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה עֹשֶׂ֤ה אֲרֻבּוֹת֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם הֲיִהְיֶ֖ה הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנְּכָ֤ה רֹאֶה֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וּמִשָּׁ֖ם לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל

verses.restored: Four men afflicted with skin disease were at entrance of gate. They said each to his neighbor, Why are we sitting here until we die?

familiar.text: And there were four leprous men at the entering in of the gate: and they said one to another, Why sit we here until we die?

modern.text: Now there were four men with leprosy at the entrance of the city gate, and they said to one another, “Why just sit here until we die?

original.text: וְאַרְבָּעָ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֛ים הָי֥וּ מְצֹרָעִ֖ים פֶּ֣תַח הַשָּׁ֑עַר וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל רֵעֵ֔הוּ מָ֗ה אֲנַ֛חְנוּ יֹשְׁבִ֥ים פֹּ֖ה עַד מָֽתְנוּ

verses.restored: If we say, Let us enter city, famine is in city and we shall die there. If we sit here, we shall die. Now therefore come, let us fall to camp of Arameans. If they preserve us alive, we shall live; and if they put us to death, we shall die.

familiar.text: If we say, We will enter into the city, then the famine is in the city, and we shall die there: and if we sit still here, we die also. Now therefore come, and let us fall unto the host of the Syrians: if they save us alive, we shall live; and if they kill us, we shall but die.

modern.text: If we say, ‘Let us go into the city,’ we will die there from the famine in the city; but if we sit here, we will also die. So come now, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they let us live, we will live; if they kill us, we will die.”

original.text: אִם אָמַרְנוּ֩ נָב֨וֹא הָעִ֜יר וְהָרָעָ֤ב בָּעִיר֙ וָמַ֣תְנוּ שָׁ֔ם וְאִם יָשַׁ֥בְנוּ פֹ֖ה וָמָ֑תְנוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה לְכוּ֙ וְנִפְּלָה֙ אֶל מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם אִם יְחַיֻּ֣נוּ נִֽחְיֶ֔ה וְאִם יְמִיתֻ֖נוּ וָמָֽתְנוּ

verses.restored: They rose in twilight to enter camp of Arameans. They came to edge of camp of Aram, and look, no man was there.

familiar.text: And they rose up in the twilight, to go unto the camp of the Syrians: and when they were come to the uttermost part of the camp of Syria, behold, there was no man there.

modern.text: So they arose at twilight and went to the camp of the Arameans. But when they came to the outskirts of the camp, there was not a man to be found.

original.text: וַיָּק֣וּמוּ בַנֶּ֔שֶׁף לָב֖וֹא אֶל מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַד קְצֵה֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵֽין שָׁ֖ם אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: For Lord had caused camp of Aram to hear sound of chariots, sound of horses, sound of a great force. They said each to his brother, Look, king of Israel hired against us kings of Hittites and kings of Egypt to come upon us.

familiar.text: For the LORD had made the host of the Syrians to hear a noise of chariots, and a noise of horses, even the noise of a great host: and they said one to another, Lo, the king of Israel hath hired against us the kings of the Hittites, and the kings of the Egyptians, to come upon us.

modern.text: For the Lord had caused the Arameans to hear the sound of chariots, horses, and a great army, so that they said to one another, “Look, the king of Israel must have hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians to attack us.”

original.text: וַאדֹנָ֞י הִשְׁמִ֣יעַ אֶת מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֗ם ק֥וֹל רֶ֨כֶב֙ ק֣וֹל ס֔וּס ק֖וֹל חַ֣יִל גָּד֑וֹל וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל אָחִ֗יו הִנֵּ֣ה שָֽׂכַר עָלֵינוּ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת מַלְכֵ֧י הַחִתִּ֛ים וְאֶת מַלְכֵ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם לָב֥וֹא עָלֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: They rose and fled in twilight, abandoned tents, horses, and donkeys—the camp as it was—and fled for their lives.

familiar.text: Wherefore they arose and fled in the twilight, and left their tents, and their horses, and their asses, even the camp as it was, and fled for their life.

modern.text: Thus the Arameans had arisen and fled at twilight, abandoning their tents and horses and donkeys. The camp was intact, and they had run for their lives.

original.text: וַיָּקוּמוּ֮ וַיָּנ֣וּסוּ בַנֶּשֶׁף֒ וַיַּעַזְב֣וּ אֶת אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם וְאֶת סֽוּסֵיהֶם֙ וְאֶת חֲמֹ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁר הִ֑יא וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ אֶל נַפְשָֽׁם

verses.restored: Those afflicted with skin disease came to edge of camp, entered one tent, ate and drank, carried from there silver, gold, and garments, went and hid them; they returned, entered another tent, carried from there, went and hid.

familiar.text: And when these lepers came to the uttermost part of the camp, they went into one tent, and did eat and drink, and carried thence silver, and gold, and raiment, and went and hid it; and came again, and entered into another tent, and carried thence also, and went and hid it.

modern.text: When the lepers reached the edge of the camp, they went into a tent to eat and drink. Then they carried off the silver, gold, and clothing, and went and hid them. On returning, they entered another tent, carried off some items from there, and hid them.

original.text: וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ הַֽמְצֹרָעִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה עַד קְצֵ֣ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אֶל אֹ֤הֶל אֶחָד֙ וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֗ם כֶּ֤סֶף וְזָהָב֙ וּבְגָדִ֔ים וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ וַיַּטְמִ֑נוּ וַיָּשֻׁ֗בוּ וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶל אֹ֣הֶל אַחֵ֔ר וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ וַיַּטְמִֽנוּ

verses.restored: They said each to his neighbor, We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until morning light, guilt will find us. Now therefore come, let us go and tell house of king.

familiar.text: Then they said one to another, We do not well: this day is a day of good tidings, and we hold our peace: if we tarry till the morning light, some mischief will come upon us: now therefore come, that we may go and tell the king’s household.

modern.text: Finally, they said to one another, “We are not doing what is right. Today is a day of good news. If we are silent and wait until morning light, our sin will overtake us. Now, therefore, let us go and tell the king’s household.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל רֵעֵ֜הוּ לֹֽא כֵ֣ן אֲנַ֣חְנוּ עֹשִׂ֗ים הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ יוֹם בְּשֹׂרָ֣ה ה֔וּא וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ מַחְשִׁ֗ים וְחִכִּ֛ינוּ עַד א֥וֹר הַבֹּ֖קֶר וּמְצָאָ֣נוּ עָו֑וֹן וְעַתָּה֙ לְכ֣וּ וְנָבֹ֔אָה וְנַגִּ֖ידָה בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: They came and called to gatekeepers of city and told them, saying, We came to camp of Aram, and look, no man there, no human voice, only horses bound, donkeys bound, and tents as they were.

familiar.text: So they came and called unto the porter of the city: and they told them, saying, We came to the camp of the Syrians, and, behold, there was no man there, neither voice of man, but horses tied, and asses tied, and the tents as they were.

modern.text: So they went and called out to the gatekeepers of the city, saying, “We went to the Aramean camp and no one was there—not a trace—only tethered horses and donkeys, and the tents were intact.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֮ אֶל שֹׁעֵ֣ר הָעִיר֒ וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לָהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֚אנוּ אֶל מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵֽין שָׁ֛ם אִ֖ישׁ וְק֣וֹל אָדָ֑ם כִּ֣י אִם הַסּ֤וּס אָסוּר֙ וְהַחֲמ֣וֹר אָס֔וּר וְאֹהָלִ֖ים כַּאֲשֶׁר הֵֽמָּה

verses.restored: Gatekeepers called, and they told it inside house of king.

familiar.text: And he called the porters; and they told it to the king’s house within.

modern.text: The gatekeepers shouted the news, and it was reported to the king’s household.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֖א הַשֹּֽׁעֲרִ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֕ידוּ בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ פְּנִֽימָה

verses.restored: King arose in night and said to his servants, Let me tell you now what Arameans did to us. They know we are hungry, so they went out from camp to hide in field, saying, When they come out from city, we will seize them alive and enter city.

familiar.text: And the king arose in the night, and said unto his servants, I will now shew you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we be hungry; therefore are they gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the field, saying, When they come out of the city, we shall catch them alive, and get into the city.

modern.text: So the king got up in the night and said to his servants, “Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know we are starving, so they have left the camp to hide in the field, thinking, ‘When they come out of the city, we will take them alive and enter the city.’”

original.text: וַיָּ֨קָם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לַ֗יְלָה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל עֲבָדָ֔יו אַגִּֽידָה נָּ֣א לָכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר עָ֥שׂוּ לָ֖נוּ אֲרָ֑ם יָדְע֞וּ כִּי רְעֵבִ֣ים אֲנַ֗חְנוּ וַיֵּצְא֤וּ מִן הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ לְהֵחָבֵ֤ה בהשדה לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי יֵצְא֤וּ מִן הָעִיר֙ וְנִתְפְּשֵׂ֣ם חַיִּ֔ים וְאֶל הָעִ֖יר נָבֹֽא

verses.restored: One of his servants answered and said, Please let men take five of remaining horses that remain in city—look, they are like all multitude of Israel that remains in it, or like all multitude of Israel that has come to an end—and let us send and see.

familiar.text: And one of his servants answered and said, Let some take, I pray thee, five of the horses that remain, which are left in the city, (behold, they are as all the multitude of Israel that are left in it: behold, I say, they are even as all the multitude of the Israelites that are consumed:) and let us send and see.

modern.text: But one of his servants replied, “Please, have scouts take five of the horses that remain in the city. Their plight will be no worse than all the Israelites who are left here. You can see that all the Israelites here are doomed. So let us send them and find out.”

original.text: וַיַּעַן֩ אֶחָ֨ד מֵעֲבָדָ֜יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר וְיִקְחוּ נָ֞א חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה מִן הַסּוּסִים֮ הַֽנִּשְׁאָרִים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאֲרוּ בָהּ֒ הִנָּ֗ם כְּכָל ההמון יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאֲרוּ בָ֔הּ הִנָּ֕ם כְּכָל הֲמ֥וֹן יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁר תָּ֑מּוּ וְנִשְׁלְחָ֖ה וְנִרְאֶֽה

verses.restored: They took two chariot teams with horses, and king sent after camp of Aram, saying, Go and see.

familiar.text: They took therefore two chariot horses; and the king sent after the host of the Syrians, saying, Go and see.

modern.text: Then the scouts took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the Aramean army, saying, “Go and see.”

original.text: וַיִּקְח֕וּ שְׁנֵ֖י רֶ֣כֶב סוּסִ֑ים וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אַחֲרֵ֧י מַחֲנֵֽה אֲרָ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר לְכ֥וּ וּרְאֽוּ

verses.restored: They went after them as far as Jordan, and look, all way was full of garments and vessels Arameans threw away in their haste. Messengers returned and told king.

familiar.text: And they went after them unto Jordan: and, lo, all the way was full of garments and vessels, which the Syrians had cast away in their haste. And the messengers returned, and told the king.

modern.text: And they tracked them as far as the Jordan, and indeed, the whole way was littered with the clothing and equipment the Arameans had thrown off in haste. So the scouts returned and told the king. Elisha’s Prophecy Fulfilled

original.text: וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ אַחֲרֵיהֶם֮ עַד הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ וְהִנֵּ֣ה כָל הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ מְלֵאָ֤ה בְגָדִים֙ וְכֵלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר הִשְׁלִ֥יכוּ אֲרָ֖ם בהחפזם וַיָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: People went out and plundered camp of Aram. A seah of fine flour was for one shekel and two seahs of barley for one shekel, according to word of YHWH.

familiar.text: And the people went out, and spoiled the tents of the Syrians. So a measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.

modern.text: Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. It was then that a seah of fine flour sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley sold for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א הָעָ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֕זּוּ אֵ֖ת מַחֲנֵ֣ה אֲרָ֑ם וַיְהִ֨י סְאָה סֹ֜לֶת בְּשֶׁ֗קֶל וְסָאתַ֧יִם שְׂעֹרִ֛ים בְּשֶׁ֖קֶל כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: King appointed officer on whose hand he leaned over gate, and people trampled him in gate, and he died, as man of Divine spoke when king came down to him.

familiar.text: And the king appointed the lord on whose hand he leaned to have the charge of the gate: and the people trode upon him in the gate, and he died, as the man of God had said, who spake when the king came down to him.

modern.text: Now the king had appointed the officer on whose arm he leaned to be in charge of the gate, but the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died, just as the man of God had foretold when the king had come to him.

original.text: וְהַמֶּלֶךְ֩ הִפְקִ֨יד אֶת הַשָּׁלִ֜ישׁ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁעָ֤ן עַל יָדוֹ֙ עַל הַשַּׁ֔עַר וַיִּרְמְסֻ֧הוּ הָעָ֛ם בַּשַּׁ֖עַר וַיָּמֹ֑ת כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּרֶ֥דֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֵלָֽיו

verses.restored: It happened according to word of man of Divine to king, saying, Two seahs of barley for one shekel and a seah of fine flour for one shekel shall be about this time tomorrow at gate of Samaria.

familiar.text: And it came to pass as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, Two measures of barley for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, shall be to morrow about this time in the gate of Samaria:

modern.text: It happened just as the man of God had told the king: “About this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria, two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel.”

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כְּדַבֵּר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶל הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר סָאתַ֨יִם שְׂעֹרִ֜ים בְּשֶׁ֗קֶל וּֽסְאָה סֹ֨לֶת֙ בְּשֶׁ֔קֶל יִהְיֶה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת מָחָ֔ר בְּשַׁ֖עַר שֹׁמְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: The officer answered man of Divine and said, Look, if YHWH made windows in heavens, could it be according to this word? He said, Look, you shall see it with your eyes, but from there you shall not eat.

familiar.text: And that lord answered the man of God, and said, Now, behold, if the LORD should make windows in heaven, might such a thing be? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.

modern.text: And the officer had answered the man of God, “Look, even if the LORD were to make windows in heaven, could this really happen?” So Elisha had replied, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it!”

verses.restored: So it happened to him: people trampled him in gate, and he died.

familiar.text: And so it fell out unto him: for the people trode upon him in the gate, and he died.

modern.text: And that is just what happened to him. The people trampled him in the gateway, and he died.

original.text: וַיְהִי ל֖וֹ כֵּ֑ן וַיִּרְמְס֨וּ אֹת֥וֹ הָעָ֛ם בַּשַּׁ֖עַר וַיָּמֹֽת

translation_notes: The four men at the gate are excluded from the besieged city because of skin disease. Their marginalization places them between starvation inside and enemy danger outside.
The term traditionally translated lepers does not securely identify Hansen's disease. Avoid contagion mythology and disability stigma.
Their decision is not reckless heroism but survival calculation under conditions where every available option may end in death.
The excluded men first eat, drink, and secure goods. Starving people meeting abundance should not be judged for immediate survival behavior.
They then recognize a duty to share good news. The people ignored by the city become the city's life-saving messengers.
The king's suspicion is rational after siege deception; verification before mass movement is prudent rather than faithlessness.
The abandoned Aramean camp becomes famine relief through plunder. This does not romanticize war economies or justify looting outside the narrative.
The officer dies by crowd trampling at the gate. His skepticism does not make crowd-crush death an acceptable punishment or prove doubters deserve harm.
Rapid food-price reversal is a narrative miracle, not an economic promise that faith guarantees cheap food or sudden market recovery.
safety_note: Do not stigmatize skin disease, excluded people, hunger behavior, or skepticism. Do not celebrate crowd-crush death or use it to threaten doubters. Center the four marginalized men as survival witnesses whose disclosure saves a city, and treat safe verification and equitable food access as essential.
